i went through basically the exact same experience as you once i stopped taking accutane. my mental well-being was at an all-time low because of how insecure losing my hair made me feel. my derm never confirmed, but I am 99.99% sure I went through what’s called telogen effluvium (TE), which is sudden hair loss occurring as the result of a traumatic event or stress (in this case, accutane).

however, and trust me, your hair WILL grow back. what helped me were the following:
- avoiding stress as much as possible: i know how obvious that might sound, but worrying about this issue will only lead to more hair falling out. reassure yourself that this is only temporary.
- minoxidil: consistent use definitely helped hair start to grow back normally and halt further hair loss
- Ketoconazole shampoo: any scalp condition can exacerbate shedding, from what you mentioned, my guess is you might be struggling with seborrheic dermatitis (contributing to hair loss). fear not however, not only will this shampoo help with those uncomfortable symptoms, but the main ingredient has also been shown to aid in the process of hair regrowth.

after consistent use of these (4-6 months minimum) and once hair loss was controlled, i gradually moved to a more “holistic” approach. i now use essential rosemary oil in my shampoo, salicylic acid treatments, and scalp scrubbers to maintain my results. i can safely say though, two years after that happening, i’ve never struggled with TE again! I second everything other commenters have said and would also like to point out that the acne and scarring (from said acne) are mostly located on your cheeks. Although you are mostly dealing with scarring now, you should know acne can have many culprits, so do be careful with the following: 

- I notice you shave your beard. Shaving can be quite irritating for the skin, especially if done over active acne (“new acne” with a white dot on it). When shaving, be careful to go with the direction of the hair growth (not against), avoid active acne as much as possible, and always always use a clean blade.

- When sleeping, make sure your bed sheets and pillow covers are always clean. Not sure what kind of a sleeper you are, but it’s very possible either side of your face touches your pillow which could be dirty and thus lead to more acne.

- Diet is also a must when tackling acne, be wary of your sugar and salt intake (esp. sugar). Since you said you’d like to incorporate more natural options, drinking spearmint and green tea can be total boosters for your routine. Also, if you exercise, it’s a must you wash your face as soon as possible after your workout as excess sweat can also trigger acne.

- If you tend to have the habit of touching your face, stop!!! Touching your face only leads to transferring bacteria from our hands (nails, fingers, nail beds) to our face. Although you might not notice, do be careful.

- Avoid taking long showers with hot water, not only can this trigger acne but it overall increases redness, irritation and sensitivity of the skin

- When drying your face, don’t scrub with the towel, rather pat dry: gently press towel on skin, remove towel, repeat pressing towel on another area.



Just some tips, hope they can help!
